name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,483

clue.text: Type of chart following tech company's typically American product

indicators.note: the chart type comes after the company's name, setting the order of the two parts

blocks.note: a pie chart shows proportions as slices

explanation.surface: A graph of sales figures trailing a big Silicon Valley firm's latest gadget.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'as American as apple pie' makes this baked dessert the emblem of anything quintessentially from the United States.

clue.text: Snake upped and left maiden in Bible verse

indicators.note: in a down entry, turned upwards means the word is read from bottom to top

blocks.note: the asp is a small venomous serpent
M is a maiden over on a cricket scorecard

explanation.surface: A serpent rises up and abandons a young woman in a scriptural passage, like Eden retold.
explanation.definitionFit: Each of the Psalms is a sacred song from the Old Testament, loosely called a verse of scripture.

clue.text: Breather during girl's gymnastic exercising

blocks.note: G is a common abbreviation for girl

explanation.surface: A young woman takes a rest break in the middle of her gym routine.
explanation.definitionFit: A lunge is a forward stride with bent knees, a standard workout move, so doing them is a form of physical training.

clue.text: Unwelcome presence of stranger, OAP off to hide soon

indicators.note: food gone off has spoiled, so these letters are corrupted into a new order
the jumbled letters conceal another word tucked inside them

explanation.surface: An unwanted stranger turns up, and a pensioner hurries off to hide from them. OAP is old-age pensioner.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin diplomatic phrase labels someone officially barred or unwelcome in a country, hence any unwanted individual.

clue.text: Result of being soused regularly

indicators.note: at regular intervals, so every other letter is taken

blocks.note: second, fourth, sixth, eighth and tenth letters

explanation.surface: The consequence of being drunk all the time, a sobering warning.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to result means to follow on as a consequence, which is exactly what this verb means.

clue.text: Scoundrel getting berth in secret service. It's just not cricket?

indicators.note: given a berth inside, so one word is lodged within another

blocks.note: a cad is a dishonourable man

explanation.surface: A rogue is given a post in the intelligence agency, behaviour that is plainly unsporting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not cricket' is the British idiom for unfair play; read literally, it describes a chirping insect that resembles a cricket but is a different creature.
explanation.definitionFit: This singing insect is often confused with the cricket but belongs to a separate order, so it is literally not one.

clue.text: Could be builder or interpreter, legally speaking, in America

blocks.note: first meaning: someone who constructs, read literally
second meaning: a US jurist who reads the Constitution a particular way

explanation.walkthrough: In US law, a 'strict constructionist' interprets the Constitution narrowly; the same word read at face value suggests a construction worker.
explanation.definitionFit: Construing a text means interpreting it, while constructing means building, and this word stretches to cover both activities.

clue.text: Deal makers meeting roughly with failures

blocks.note: C is short for circa, about

explanation.surface: Salespeople mixing it up with people who never succeed.
explanation.definitionFit: In sales jargon, the person who clinches an agreement is said to close it, so successful negotiators earn this name.

clue.text: Flawed policeman brings in female and removes shirt

indicators.note: a new letter is introduced into the word
and another letter is taken out to make room

explanation.surface: A dodgy officer brings in a woman and takes off his top, a scandal in the making.
explanation.walkthrough: The T of the officer's title is swapped for F.
explanation.definitionFit: Something faulty or imperfect has a defect, so the adjective means not working properly.

clue.text: One who outlaws hanging

blocks.note: first meaning: a person who prohibits things, read whimsically
second meaning: a long cloth sign hung up for display

explanation.surface: A judge who outlaws, ordering an execution by rope.
explanation.definitionFit: A cloth strip hung across a street or wall is a common noun sense; one who forbids things is a playful agent noun.

clue.text: Senator removes hat to make goodbyes

blocks.note: to doff is to lift or take off a hat

explanation.surface: A politician tips their hat in farewell as they leave.
explanation.definitionFit: Farewell parties or ceremonies for departing people are called by this hyphenated plural noun.

clue.text: All-powerful men opt into corruption

indicators.note: corrupted text is mangled, so these letters are spoiled into another order

explanation.surface: Absolute power tempts men to choose corruption, as Lord Acton warned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Into' looks like a link but is part of the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A Latin-derived word for having unlimited authority or might, usually said of God.

clue.text: Score and more, getting husband

explanation.surface: Twenty, and then some more, plus a husband thrown in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Score' poses as the number twenty; it is the verb meaning to scratch a line.
explanation.definitionFit: To score a surface is to cut lines into it, just as an engraver cuts a design into metal or glass.

clue.text: Underworld set alight

blocks.note: a bird alights when it comes down to rest

explanation.surface: Hades has been set on fire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set alight' reads as arson; split, set is a group and alight means to settle.
explanation.definitionFit: The criminal world of organised mobs is called the underworld, and this word names that same territory.

clue.text: Despise a failure (but not another 7, by the sound of it)

indicators.note: the phrase is judged by how it is spoken, not how it is written

blocks.note: a flop or dud is a bomb
the bracket points past entry 7 to the number eight

explanation.surface: Loathe a flop, though not a second one of the 7 kind.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud the answer is 'a bomb in eight'; the bracket's cross-reference is the setter's roundabout way to the number eight rather than seven.
explanation.definitionFit: To loathe or detest intensely, a formal verb for feeling strong hatred toward someone or something.

clue.text: It goes with a dash of pepper

blocks.note: first meaning: the short signal paired with the long one in Morse code
second meaning: to sprinkle or scatter over a surface

explanation.walkthrough: 'A dash of pepper' is a cooking measure; split, the dash is from Morse code and pepper is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Morse code pairs short and long signals, and to sprinkle points over something is to pepper it.

clue.text: International organisation's emergency relief not conveyed

blocks.note: the UN, with its possessive S

explanation.surface: Relief from the United Nations that never reaches the people it was meant for.
explanation.definitionFit: Words left unspoken were never put across or expressed, which is what conveyed would mean for a message.

clue.text: Cocktail giving Italian a veneer of sexual attraction

indicators.note: a veneer is a thin outer layer, so one word coats the other

blocks.note: mojo is personal magnetism or sex appeal

explanation.surface: A drink that lends an Italian man a superficial air of charm.
explanation.definitionFit: A Cuban rum drink with mint, lime and soda, one of the best-known mixed drinks.

clue.text: Diseased bird expressly prohibited

indicators.note: to express is to put into spoken words, so the phrase is heard rather than read

blocks.note: a sick bird of prey: ill plus eagle

explanation.surface: A sick bird of prey that the law explicitly forbids keeping.
explanation.definitionFit: Something forbidden by statute is against the law, the plain meaning of this adjective.

clue.text: Bear traps in place, secured with rope

indicators.note: something trapped is held inside, so one word encloses the other

explanation.surface: A bear pins something in position, held fast by a line.
explanation.definitionFit: An animal tied to a post by a line or chain is kept from straying, which is what this past participle describes.

clue.text: Finished with old flame before pride damaged

indicators.note: the first part comes ahead of the second
damaged things are knocked out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Done with a former lover after one's ego takes a knock.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that has run out or come to its end, like a passport past its date, is over.

clue.text: Going through litre bottle

explanation.surface: Getting through a whole litre bottle.
explanation.definitionFit: A small glass container for liquids such as medicine or perfume is a kind of little flask.

clue.text: Spirit involved in delusional state

explanation.surface: A ghost caught up in a disordered mind.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who believes they are infallible or all-powerful is said to suffer from this psychological condition.

clue.text: Who's enemy of the king beyond the valley?

indicators.note: the monarch comes after, further along than the other part

blocks.note: a dale is a valley, especially in northern England
K is king in chess notation

explanation.surface: Asking who the king's foe is, lurking past the valley.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Who' is the Doctor in the long-running British TV series Doctor Who.
explanation.definitionFit: These pepper-pot shaped cyborgs are the Doctor's most famous adversaries in the science-fiction drama.

clue.text: People employed by editor to edit

indicators.note: staff employed by a firm are inside it, so one word goes within the other

explanation.surface: Staff hired by a newspaper boss to correct copy.
explanation.definitionFit: To correct and revise a text is to make it right, which is what this verb means.

clue.text: Put up picture with tack, getting finger injury

blocks.note: you hang a picture on a wall

explanation.surface: Hanging a picture with a tack and hurting a finger in the process.
explanation.definitionFit: A painful torn strip of skin beside a fingernail is a small but nagging hand complaint.

clue.text: Realist curtailed reforms in Middle East country

indicators.note: cut short at the tail, so the final letter goes
to re-form is to shape again, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A pragmatic politician scales back their plans for change in a troubled region.
explanation.definitionFit: This state on the eastern Mediterranean coast is a nation of the region named.

clue.text: Remove parasites from ale-fed vagrant

indicators.note: a vagrant wanders about, so these letters roam into a new order

explanation.surface: Delousing a beer-soaked tramp.
explanation.definitionFit: Ridding a pet of the small jumping insects that bite it removes those bloodsucking pests.

clue.text: Children round at yard in chirpy jumpers

indicators.note: going round something encircles it

explanation.surface: Kids in a playground wearing cheerful sweaters. A jumper is a British sweater.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jumpers' suggests knitwear; here it means leaping insects.
explanation.definitionFit: These green North American bush crickets leap about and make loud calls, so they are chirping hoppers.
